title: Mortgage Covenant on Insurance — Hazard and Flood Coverage for Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
## Covenant

1. **Hazard insurance.** Where the appraised value of insurable buildings on the parcels mortgaged to a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage exceeds the product's buildings insurance threshold, hazard insurance naming the association mortgagee must be kept in force.
2. **Flood insurance.** Buildings in a special flood hazard area must carry flood insurance for the lesser of the building value and the National Flood Insurance Program maximum for the building type.
3. **Lapse of flood coverage.** When coverage is not in force, the member is notified and, if proof is not received by the end of the product's flood notice period in calendar days after the notice date, the association force-places flood coverage and assesses its premium as a flood insurance fee.
4. **Late proof.** Proof of coverage effective on or before the force-placement date, received later, waives that premium as an error correction.
5. **Bare land.** Bare land without buildings carries no insurance requirement.

## National Flood Insurance Program building maximums

| Building type | Maximum (USD) |
|---|---|
| Residential | 250000.00 |
| Non-residential | 500000.00 |

## Required flood coverage (hypothetical buildings in a special flood hazard area)

| Building | Building value (USD) | Program maximum (USD) | Required coverage (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Farm residence | 320000 | 250000 | 250000 |
| Machine shed | 180000 | 500000 | 180000 |
| Grain handling building | 640000 | 500000 | 500000 |

## Notice period (hypothetical dates)

With a 45-day notice period and a notice dated 1 April 2026, proof received by the end of 16 May 2026 (the forty-fifth calendar day after the notice date) prevents force-placement. If no proof is received by then, coverage is force-placed and its premium assessed; if proof of coverage effective on or before the force-placement date arrives afterwards, the premium is waived as an error correction.
